title: Nonergodicity from Hilbert-Subspace Cloning
abstract: We identify a class of nonintegrable quantum many-body systems composed of single Pauli strings that possess an extensive number of noncommuting local conserved quantities and exhibit partial ergodicity breaking due to exponentially degenerate energy spectra. We show that such systems exhibit a novel mechanism, Hilbert-subspace cloning, where the identical chaotic Hamiltonian acts on each of exponentially many disconnected Hilbert subspaces. Although the dynamics within each clone thermalizes, quantum coherence between clones remains protected and detectable by local observables. Consequently, the long-time behavior of local observables is described by a coherence-preserving partial Gibbs ensemble, where the hidden subsystem retains its initial quantum coherence.
summary: This paper analyzes quantum many-body systems exhibiting Hilbert-subspace cloning, where the Hamiltonian acts on many disconnected, yet identical, subspaces. Despite the chaotic dynamics within each subspace, the global system fails to fully thermalize because quantum coherence between these subspaces is protected. The long-time state is thus described by a coherence-preserving partial Gibbs ensemble.
main_problem: The paper investigates how exponentially large spectral degeneracies in quantum many-body systems can lead to nonergodicity, protecting quantum coherence from local thermalization.
main_result: The system exhibits Hilbert-subspace cloning, leading to a long-time steady state described by a coherence-preserving partial Gibbs ensemble, which differs from the standard thermal ensemble.
method: The authors analyze the structure imposed by local conserved quantities, applying concepts from quantum chaos (GOE statistics) and testing for thermalization using the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH).
model_or_system: The model is a single-Pauli-string (SPS) system on a 1D lattice of spin-1/2 spins, governed by a Hamiltonian constructed from Pauli strings. The system decomposes into exponentially many disconnected, yet identical, subspaces.
key_observables: Local observables, level spacing ratio distribution (GOE confirmation), and expectation values of local Pauli strings in eigenstates.
important_parameters: The system size L, the coupling strengths (implicit in the Pauli strings), and the temperature/inverse temperature $ eta$ (implied by the Gibbs ensemble).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of ETH for the individual subspace Hamiltonians $H(\lambda)$ and focuses on the inversion-asymmetric case.
figures_summary: Figure 2 shows level spacing ratios following the GOE distribution, confirming quantum chaoticity. Figure 3 shows the expectation value of local operators converging smoothly, confirming ETH.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the block-diagonal structure due to conserved quantities, then uses chaos diagnostics (level spacing) to confirm the chaotic nature of the individual subspaces. Finally, it analyzes the long-time dynamics, showing the deviation from standard thermalization towards a coherence-preserving partial Gibbs state.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical mechanism (HSC) for non-equilibrium steady states in quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding quantum memory and information storage in complex many-body settings.
